controls_available: Simplified roster controls: individual worker or soldier buttons plus WORKERS, SOLDIERS, and CLEAR selection buttons.
GATHER sends the selected workers to the visible seed pile.
SCOUT sends exactly one selected worker to the visible listening front until contact is acquired.
EXCAVATE sends exactly two selected workers to the brood chamber; RAISE consumes two seeds and queues one soldier.
MARCH NORTH and MARCH SOUTH commit the selected soldiers to the active raid's branch; ASSAULT RIVAL sends selected soldiers to the enemy queen after every raid is cleared.
CERTIFY FRONT is administrative and does not affect the outcome.
autonomous_processes: The live page advances the simulation from elapsed performance time in 100 ms ticks, including while no new command is supplied.
A deployed scout completes after 40 ticks and reveals contact; exactly two diggers add two brood-progress units per tick until 70 work, after which they gather automatically.
Gatherers add one seed every 18 ticks, and each RAISE order produces a soldier after 14 ticks.
At difficulty 3 the single seeded raid builds from tick 105 to 168, spawns at tick 180, travels toward the queen, and reaches its 219-259 response band before impact at tick 270.

During the response band the raid formation's visible vertical position follows a phase-offset sinusoid with a 36-tick period; at impact the committed lane and the surviving committed soldiers determine whether the four-raider wave is stopped.
After the raid is resolved, an enemy assault takes 45 ticks to reach and damage the rival queen; the fixed CSS pulse is presentation-only and is not part of the task state.

clause_i.reason: For the moving-raid defense mode, I_t contains only the reviewer's prior commands and their task times. The generator independently randomizes the first raid lane and a 0-35 tick motion phase offset across instances. Thus the same prior command/tick history can lead to different NORTH/SOUTH actions being optimal at t+Delta. A fixed q(I_t) must choose the same branch for both, and no-op or the wrong branch cannot stop all four raiders, so it cannot be optimal for every history in C_Delta(D).

clause_ii.reason: The six chronological frames in the configured 800 ms window expose the red formation's changing vertical position and advance direction on the visible canvas/minimap. The rendered phase-offset sinusoid has a known 36-tick period, so the recent trajectory predicts which branch will be correct when the command is delivered eight ticks later. The simplified NORTH/SOUTH command buttons and roster remain visible, and the supplied screenshot-only solver samples successive formation images and maps downward/upward motion to SOUTH/NORTH. This supplies a bounded g(I_t,W_t^w) without private state.

clause_iii.reason: Choose a history in the active 219-259 response band with the formation approaching a vertical turning point, and choose Delta=800 ms so t+Delta is still before tick 259. Within some tau<Delta the visible sinusoidal motion crosses the sign change used by interceptLane; the same MARCH branch remains a valid control but becomes the wrong, strictly less effective commitment. At impact only correctly committed soldiers in the committed lane stop the wave; a wrong commitment stops none and removes four queen HP, while the opposite branch still leaves success possible. The strict loss is caused by the changing raid state, not by a deadline or later completion.

common_visible_process: The common D is the simplified command-panel defense commitment for the one seeded wave. After the scout reveals contact, the rendered four-ant formation moves horizontally toward the colony and vertically as a phase-offset sinusoid during the visible intercept band. The same visible motion supplies the recent evidence needed to extrapolate the branch at t+800 ms, changes which MARCH target is optimal, and changes the impact result through the grader's correct-commitment test.

pre_run.reason: Every difficulty-3 instance has one four-raider wave. A successful replay requires an outcome-affecting NORTH/SOUTH commitment during that wave's response band, and the UI/grader reject MARCH -> enemy until every raid has resolved, requiring a separate outcome-affecting assault afterward. Therefore no instance has a successful continuation that starts one autonomous outcome phase and sends no further outcome-affecting actions through that phase; the 50% pre-run override is not met. The exact rate is left null rather than invented because a seed census was unnecessary for this structural exclusion.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 3 is the medium five-worker/two-worker excavation configuration with one four-raider seeded wave, 180/270 spawn and impact ticks, hidden opening, and the simplified labelled-roster/explicit-order interface; the observation window is 800 ms with six frames.
The environment exposes frame-window observations, mouse and keyboard actions, an 800 ms observation window, six frames per observation, and a 100 ms simulation tick in the live runner.
